The House of Representatives on Tuesday, May 5, 2026, approved on third and final reading House Bill No. 8581, which seeks to establish a polytechnic institute in Polangui, Albay. INQUIRER FILES

LEGAZPI CITY, Albay — The House of Representatives on Tuesday approved on third and final reading House Bill No. 8581, which seeks to establish a polytechnic institute in Polangui, Albay.

The proposed “Polangui Polytechnic Institute” was principally authored by Albay 3rd District Rep. Raymond Adrian E. Salceda.

Salceda said the measure, once enacted, will benefit Filipinos by serving as a center for advanced technical-vocational education, lifelong learning, and trainer development programs under the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) in the Bicol Region.

Article continues after this 

The measure seeks to address the lack of advanced training, trainer upgrading, and continuing education amid rapid changes in technology and industry, he said.

He added that many existing training centers focus mainly on entry-level skills, limiting workers’ opportunities for higher qualifications and specialized training.

World.title: Bohol eyes conversion of provincial roads into national roads
World.content:
Bohol Gov. Erico Aristotle Aumentado holds a meeting with DPWH Sec. Vince Dizon in Manila on May 5, 2026, for the conversion of several provincial roads in Bohol into national roads —Photo courtesy of Bohol Capitol

TAGBILARAN CITY, Bohol — Around 29 provincial roads in Bohol are being pushed for conversion into national roads as the provincial government seeks stronger support from the national government for infrastructure development.

Gov. Erico Aristotle Aumentado said the move was discussed during a meeting with Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon in Manila.

According to Aumentado, converting provincial roads into national roads would allow the DPWH to allocate funds for the roads’ improvement, rehabilitation, and maintenance.

Article continues after this 

READ: House OKs land use act on 3rd reading

“Our meeting with DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon here in Manila was productive, where we pushed for the conversion of several provincial roads in Bohol into national roads, ” Aumentado said.

He explained that once the roads are classified as national roads, the national government could provide funding support through the DPWH.

The proposed road conversions, endorsed by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, cover several strategic routes across the province.

Area 1 includes roads linking the towns of Corella, Balilihan, Baclayon, San Isidro, Catigbian, Antequera, Alburquerque, Maribojoc, Loon, and nearby junction roads connecting major provincial corridors.

Article continues after this 

Area 2 covers road networks linking San Miguel, Ubay, Danao, Inabanga, Buenavista, Alicia, Getafe, Mabini, Trinidad, Bien Unido, and Pres. Carlos P. Garcia, including access roads leading to ports and wharves that support inter-island and local transport connectivity.

Area 3 includes routes connecting Loboc, Sevilla, Guindulman, Pilar, Bilar, Candijay, Anda and Sikatuna, improving access to interior and eastern towns in the province.

Article continues after this 

READ: DA readies changes in land conversion rules

Additional roads proposed for conversion include the San Miguel–Kauswagan–Magsaysay road leading to Cangmundo in Getafe; the San Vicente–Estaca–Taming route connecting Dagohoy and Danao; the Candelaria road linking Pilar and Sierra Bullones; and the Talibon–San Isidro–Nueva Esperanza Bridge corridor connecting Bien Unido to Ubay.

World.title: Cyberlibel raps vs ex-Pangasinan solon, radio personality dismissed
World.content:
The City Prosecution Office in Dagupan City has dismissed the cyberlibel, slander, and other charges filed by a local vlogger against former Pangasinan 4th District Rep. Christopher de Venecia and radio personality Violy Valdez Ferrer. —Screenshot from Wikipedia

DAGUPAN CITY, Pangasinan – The City Prosecution Office here has dismissed the cyberlibel, slander, and other charges filed by a local vlogger against former Pangasinan 4th District Rep. Christopher de Venecia and radio personality Violy Valdez Ferrer.

The resolution of the case, docketed as NPS 1-10-INV-251-00368, included charges of grave threats, perjury, falsification, obstruction of justice, and contempt. It was dated March 31, but respondents received the document only on Thursday.

Prosecutor Victoria Datuin-Cabrera said the cyber libel case against de Venecia, who shared a radio station’s social media post, failed because “personal liability for cyber libel is generally limited to the author of the post.”

Article continues after this 

Local vlogger Jaime Aquino had filed obstruction of justice and contempt charges against de Venecia after the latter shared on his Facebook page a post by Aksyon Radyo containing a certificate from the Office of the Ombudsman stating that there were no plunder and misconduct cases against him involving alleged ghost projects.

READ: Toff de Venecia: Ombudsman has cleared me of flood mess allegations

“De Venecia is not the author, editor, or administrator of the Aksyon Radyo Facebook page. His act of securing an Ombudsman clearance and the subsequent reporting thereof by a media outlet is a factual occurrence. No evidence was presented to show that he dictated the script or controlled the broadcast of respondent Ferrer,” the resolution stated.

On the charges of perjury, falsification, and obstruction of justice filed against de Venecia after he secured an Ombudsman clearance, the prosecution office said there was no evidence of a deliberate false statement on a material matter.

“The conflicting interpretations of an Ombudsman ‘clearance’ versus ‘status’ constitute a legal dispute, not a criminal lie,” the resolution stated.

Article continues after this 

READ: No ‘ghost’ flood control projects in my district – de Venecia

The prosecution office also said it had no jurisdiction over the contempt charge, noting that such matters “must be addressed to the sound discretion of the court where the alleged misbehavior occurred.”

Article continues after this 

Aquino also filed charges against Ferrer after she reportedly said on her radio program that his claim of being president of a transport group had no basis, that he had been removed from a national news organization, and that he fabricated rape allegations against former Secretary Raul Lambino that the court later dismissed.

Ferrer also allegedly told Aquino on air, “Maghanda ka baka may mangyari sa’yo,” which Aquino claimed constituted grave threats.

World.title: Colmenares: Meralco ‘bill shock’ a form of ‘legalized robbery’
World.content:
INQUIRER FILES

MANILA, Philippines — Former Bayan Muna Rep. Neri Colmenares has condemned the “bill shock” experienced by millions of electricity consumers in April and May, as rates rose to a record-high P14.35 per kilowatt-hour.

Colmenares, who described the situation as a form of “legalized robbery” against ordinary Filipinos, called on Manila Electric Co. (Meralco) to renegotiate all power supply agreements with coal and gas plants to make them “peso-denominated” instead of “dollar-indexed.”

For the former lawmaker, it is unacceptable for consumers to shoulder the burden when the peso weakens because of what he described as “dollar-denominated contracts.”

Article continues after this 

RELATED STORY: Meralco hikes rates for 3rd straight month

“Why are the people being made to pay for the peso’s depreciation?” he asked, saying that while Meralco “earns billions,” the risk is passed on to Filipino households already struggling with poverty.

He also criticized the imposition of the 12-percent value-added tax on the system loss charge, likening it to “buying goods in a market, where consumers take something home in exchange for the tax they pay.”

Colmenares said: “In system loss, you pay 12% VAT—but what do you take home? Nothing. You’re paying for electricity you didn’t even use—electricity lost due to Meralco’s inefficiency or illegal connections that they should be resolving.”

“It’s not our fault—why are we the ones being charged?” he added.

Article continues after this 

INQUIRER.net sought Meralco’s comment on Colmenares’ statement but has yet to receive a response. In a previous statement, however, Meralco said the increase was triggered by higher electricity generation costs due to rising oil prices.

RELATED STORY: Explainer: What’s driving the latest spike in electricity prices

Article continues after this 

Colmenares also criticized Meralco’s slow transition to renewable energy, saying that while some distribution cooperatives in Iloilo, Bohol and Davao have lower rates because of local and renewable energy sources, Meralco remains heavily dependent on imported natural gas and coal.

“Only 10% of Meralco’s energy is renewable,” he said.

He said the rest comes from imported gas and coal paid in dollars.

“That’s why every movement in the world market results in bill shock for consumers. This is the consequence of a monopoly reliant on foreign interests,” Colmenares said.

READ: ERC: Meralco ‘bill shock’ just follows the law

For Bayan Muna, the VAT should be removed from system loss and other pass-through charges, and government resources should be used to subsidize lifeline rates instead of passing these costs on to regular consumers.

RELATED STORY: Aquino, Hontiveros seek probe into Meralco fees

World.title: Curlee Discaya back in Senate detention after surgery
World.content:
Pacifico “Curlee” Discaya (Noy Morcoso/INQUIRER.net)

MANILA, Philippines — Government contractor Pacifico “Curlee” Discaya was returned to the Senate detention facility on Thursday after undergoing surgery.

In a message to reporters, Senate Secretary Mark Mendoza said Discaya arrived at the Senate to continue his recovery.

“Nakabalik na kaninang umaga si Mr. Discaya sa Senate, he is OK and was cleared by his doctors to continue his recovery sa Senate,” Mendoza stated.

READ: Curlee Discaya to undergo shoulder surgery

World.title: Legarda joins son’s call to probe gov’t aid distribution in Batangas
World.content:
Sen. Loren Legarda FILE PHOTO

MANILA, Philippines – Sen. Loren Legarda has joined her lawmaker-son’s call for a congressional probe into the implementation and delivery of government cash aid and subsidy programs, citing in particular the alleged unfair distribution in certain barangays in their province in Batangas.

Her proposed inquiry was contained in Senate Resolution No. 381, which she filed on Monday, May 4. Her son, Batangas 1st District Rep. Leandro Leviste, has made a similar push in the House of Representatives.

In her resolution, the senator noted various reports indicating that “beneficiaries have, in certain instances, been compelled to line up in crowded, prolonged, and inadequately managed conditions” just to get the government’s financial aid.

Article continues after this 

Legarda likewise pointed to alleged delays and logistical inefficiencies, including reports of prolonged queuing, incomplete lists, and the slow release of the fuel subsidy program to public utility drivers.

“Such incidents raise serious concerns on whether the current practice in government cash assistance and subsidy programs requiring large numbers of beneficiaries to physically line up for validation or payout is humane, safe, efficient, and consistent with the purpose of emergency relief,” she said.

She also cited the reported exclusion of at least 84 barangays in the municipalities of Taal and Nasugbu in Batangas from the barangay assistance distribution under the “Bawat Barangay Makikinabang” Program.

This, notwithstanding official statements that all barangays were to receive funding and despite their timely submission of the required documents, Legarda said, citing the same report.

“Further reports suggest that such exclusion may have been influenced by local political considerations or other non-objective factors; photographs from the said distribution also show that the rice packs distributed to beneficiaries bore the logos of the Executive Secretary and the provincial government, as well as accompanying slogans, underscoring the need to ensure that assistance programs are implemented based on clear, uniform, and non-partisan criteria,” she added.

Article continues after this 

The senator also suggested comparing the implementation of the “Bawat Barangay Makikinabang” Program in other provinces “to determine whether similar practices involving the use of logos and slogans were also adopted and to ensure that such practices are not continued.”

Questions on the implementation of the “Bawat Barangay Makikinabang” Program were first raised by the senator’s son.

Article continues after this 

READ: Leviste hits exclusion of 84 Batangas barangays in aid distribution

Leviste initially claimed that the 84 barangays were not invited to the financial subsidy distribution program in Batangas City led by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. late last month, where each barangay in the province was supposed to receive a P200,000 financial assistance package.

READ: Marcos vows to boost Local Government Support Fund

The congressman said the excluded barangays received their financial aid only after he raised the issue.

“But the president should still ask Secretary Recto and Governor Recto why they did not include these barangays today, so this abuse of public funds will not be repeated. This is also a reason why, instead of giving more ayuda, the President should just suspend the fuel excise tax and lower the VAT (value-added tax),” Leviste was also quoted as saying in media reports.

He was apparently referring to Executive Secretary Ralph Recto, who is married to incumbent Batangas Governor Vilma Santos.
